summary: Discovery call focused on Verdant Health's latency and throughput needs for a real-time clinical summarization feature. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) options. Key constraints: p95 target ~200ms for streaming completions for short responses, burst concurrency up to 150 users (approx 60 concurrent streaming requests), strict security (SOC2, KMS), and cost sensitivity for high token volumes. Agreed next step: run pilot benchmark on Dedicated with sample payloads.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (CTO - Verdant), Rohit Singh (ML Eng), Sara Ahmed (Platform Eng), Jon Reyes (Head of IT)

Summary (auto): Focus on latency/throughput, p95 & streaming, benchmarking plan, security questions around KMS/SSO/VPC.

[00:00] Alex: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood here, AE on the account. we got Priya and Daniel from our SE team. how are you all?
[00:08] Maya: Hi thanks! Maya here, excited to dig in. we have Rohit and Sara as well.
[00:12] Rohit: Hey. sorry running a bit late.
[00:15] Priya: No worries. quick agenda: first understand your latency p95 targets and concurrency, then architecture constraints (VPC/KMS), then propose benchmark plan and next steps. sound ok?
[00:28] Maya: sounds good. high level: Verdant is building a clinical note summarization feature — real-time-ish — doctors expect near instant streaming of a summary as dictation happens. our SLO is p95 around 150-250ms for short responses (single-turn, ~50-150 tokens), and we want to support bursts of up to 150 active users, which maps to roughly 50-70 concurrent streaming requests in practice.
[00:52] Daniel: ok that's super helpful. is the 150-250ms p95 for first token or for completion?
[00:58] Maya: primarily for completion of the short summary chunk. first token latency also matters but completion p95 is our customer-facing SLA.
[01:05] Priya: got it. and what is your expected tokens/sec per user during these bursts? are you doing continuous streaming?
[01:13] Rohit: yes streaming. average throughput per active session is around 20-40 tokens/sec when the doc is speaking; but summaries are usually in 50-150 token segments, so we'll see sustained token generation for 1-5 seconds.
[01:27] Sara: also we have strict data policies — PHI. so we need SOC2, audit logs, and KMS integration. Private deployment (VPC) is preferable but we're evaluating Dedicated if that meets network & compliance needs.
[01:40] Alex: good context. question on cost sensitivity — are you looking at hosted pay-as-you-go for initial phase or committed dedicated capacity?
[01:48] Maya: we'd prefer hosted for quick iteration but if Dedicated buys down latency and gives predictable costs we could move there. Private on-prem is a stretch but could be required for certain hospitals.
[01:58] Priya: for p95 150-250ms for completion at 50-70 concurrent streaming reqs, that pushes toward Dedicated or a tuned Hosted profile. some of this depends on model choice and quantization. which model family are you evaluating?
[02:12] Rohit: right now we mostly use a smaller open LLM for summarization, like a finetuned Llama-70b quantized, but we're exploring smaller 13/7b variants. latency varies a lot. we want to benchmark tokens/sec on real payloads.
[02:28] Daniel: makes sense — kernel selection and batch sizing matter. rough rule: Dedicated with pinned GPU pools reduces cold-starts and gives more consistent p95. hosted can be ok if you use a lower-latency variant or Redwood's fast paths + prefix caching.
[02:43] Maya: can you explain prefix caching / KV cache? we've heard the term but not clear on impact for streaming.
[02:49] Priya: sure — simple explanation: if parts of the prompt are repeated (system prompt, patient metadata), Redwood keeps KV cache to avoid recomputing past key/values. that can cut token compute by 30-60% depending on repetition, and for streaming it reduces time per token. but if your prompts are unique per user, benefit is less. also note caching interacts with privacy — full cache is okay in Dedicated/Private with isolation.
[03:11] Sara: ok good. on security: does Redwood support customer-managed KMS and SAML SSO? we need audit logs for all inference requests.
[03:20] Alex: yes — Redwood Private offers customer-managed KMS, and Dedicated can integrate with KMS via our key wrapping or customer-key options, and SAML SSO for console access. we provide request-level audit logs and can increase retention as an add-on. we'll share SOC2 + security pack.
[03:35] Jon: network-wise we'd need VPC peering or private link to avoid public egress for PHI. any gotchas?
[03:42] Priya: VPC peering or customer VPC with private endpoints is supported. for Dedicated we usually provision in your cloud account or peered network. need to validate firewall rules and MTU but it's standard.
[03:53] Maya: great. back to perf: do you have benchmarks for p95 with streaming? we tried some pub benchmarks but results vary.
[04:00] Daniel: we have internal perf profiles — we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet. but two important knobs: concurrency and batching. for streaming small segments, batching can't always amortize overhead, so per-request latency matters. we recommend a benchmark that mirrors your sample payloads and concurrency bursts.
[04:20] Rohit: what about token/sec numbers? for example, for a 13B quantized model, what tokens/sec can we expect per GPU?
[04:27] Priya: ballpark: a well-optimized 13B on A10-like hardware with quantization might do 150-400 tokens/sec depending on sequence length and attention optimizations. 70b families are lower for token/sec. but these numbers vary by kernel and compilation.
[04:44] Maya: those ranges help. if we need p95 200ms for 100 tokens completion, that implies 500 tokens/sec effective which seems high. maybe our segments are smaller.
[04:55] Rohit: yes our typical summary is ~80 tokens. so to complete in 200ms you'd need 400 tokens/sec. seems aggressive.
[05:03] Alex: right — that's why we often split latency goals: first-token p95 (fast streaming start) and completion p95. for streaming UX, immediate token streaming feels fast even if completion p95 is slightly higher.
[05:16] Maya: ok — UX team can relax completion to 250-300ms if first-token is <100ms.
[05:23] Daniel: excellent — that makes Dedicated more feasible. Also consider model quantization profiles: Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization + kernel combos to hit latency without huge cost.
[05:36] Priya: quick question on fallback: do you need multi-model fallbacks if capacity constrained? we can configure routing policies to prefer lower-cost models first and fallback to higher-capacity variants for SLOs.
[05:46] Maya: yes fallback is important. some hospitals require 99.9% availability under surge.
[05:51] Sara: on observability, can we get per-route token/latency breakdowns? we need to tie cost to endpoints.
[05:57] Alex: yep console has per-route and model breakdowns, token-level cost, tracing hooks. we'll send screenshots.
[06:06] Rohit: for the pilot, we want to run a token/sec benchmark that simulates 60 concurrent streaming sessions with ~80-token responses and the same prompt per session and another test with unique prompts to measure KV cache impact.
[06:20] Priya: perfect. we'll prepare two configs: repeated-prompt (to show KV cache win) and unique-prompt (worst-case). we'll run them on Dedicated and Hosted profiles so you can compare.
[06:30] Maya: timeline? we'd like results before next week. can Redwood run the pilot on 2026-06-23?
[06:36] Alex: tentative yes. need to confirm capacity and access. Priya, can you coordinate scheduling?
[06:41] Priya: yes I'll send a scheduler invite and benchmark template.
[06:44] Daniel: one more note — streaming SLOs can be sensitive to tail latency introduced by network jitter. recommend colocating inference in the same region as your app and using private networking.
[06:56] Jon: understood. our primary region is us-east-1.
[07:00] Alex: we'll note that.
[07:04] [Pause / cross-talk as people check links]
[07:20] Maya: quick question on encryption in transit at rest — we need proofs for audit.
[07:24] Alex: we'll include the security pack with KMS details, encryption-at-rest, TLS requirements, and SOC2 artifacts.
[07:32] Rohit: any concerns about model weights residency if we go private?
[07:36] Priya: in Private and Dedicated modes you can control residency. for Private on-prem we do not persist weights outside your cluster. in Dedicated we can run in your VPC so weights never touch public infra. there are nuances — we'll document.
[07:50] Maya: great. regarding pricing, do you have a sample for high-volume token workloads?
[07:55] Alex: yes we'll send a pricing sheet and a sample cost model comparing hosted pay-as-you-go vs committed Dedicated. Dedicated tends to lower unit cost at steady-state but requires commit.
[08:06] Sara: and any add-on costs for extended audit logs?
[08:09] Alex: yes audit retention and extended logs are add-ons. we'll include them in the pricing sheet.
[08:15] Rohit: in the benchmark I'd like to track p50/p95/p99 token latencies and total tokens/sec aggregated.
[08:22] Daniel: we'll include those metrics in the benchmark report and a raw CSV we share.
[08:26] Maya: ok, any blockers from Redwood side to run the test? what do you need from us?
[08:31] Priya: sample payloads (json lines), concurrency profile (how sessions ramp), and a VPN/VPC endpoint for Dedicated if you want private networking. also credentials for any test S3 where we can drop results.
[08:43] Maya: we'll share payloads and a ramp chart by 2026-06-20.
[08:47] Alex: perfect.
[08:50] [10 minute technical interlude where Priya and Daniel talk through kernel options and quantization details; transcript picks back up]
[18:55] Priya: ...so for attention optimizations, depending on sequence length we might pick different kernels; our compiler chooses at runtime but for very tight p95 you can pin a kernel and quantization profile. this reduces variability.
[19:12] Rohit: there's sometimes weird transcribe issues where 'KV cache' becomes 'KV cahce' in our notes, heh.
[19:18] Daniel: yes the export sometimes has small typos.
[19:22] Maya: fine as long as the data's good.
[19:26] Priya: for the pilot config we'll include both pinned-kernel and auto mode.
[19:32] Rohit: on the data side, can you guarantee logs won't include PHI? we need to redact or disable retention for production.
[19:39] Alex: yes in Dedicated/Private you control log retention and can disable the ingestion of raw text into shared analytics. we'll document options.
[19:48] Sara: any SLA numbers you can commit to for Dedicated?
[19:51] Alex: Dedicated SLAs include uptime and latency percentiles for provisioned throughput — we'll surface the draft SLA in the next email.
[19:59] Maya: good. one final question: do you support function calling / structured output when streaming? we rely on structured results for downstream ingestion.
[20:07] Daniel: yes function/tool calling works with streaming. we can emit structured chunks; it's tested in our runtime. there are edge cases but we can demo.
[20:16] Maya: awesome.
[20:20] Alex: ok quick recap and next steps: Alex will send pricing, SOC2/security pack, and a benchmark spreadsheet; Priya will prepare benchmark configs and schedule the run on 2026-06-23 (tentative); Verdant to provide payloads/ramp. action items captured. any other issues?
[20:39] Jon: none from infra side.
[20:43] Maya: thanks all. looking forward to the benchmark.
[20:47] Alex: thanks everyone we'll follow up via email and send calendar invites.
[20:51] [call ends]

Notes: transcript has occasional typos and imperfect speaker attribution (Fireflies auto labels). Shared artifacts referenced: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/verdant-template), security pack (link: https://redwood.app/security/pack.pdf).
